newsitem.title: UK: LLOYDS, BANKS HIT BY PROFIT TAKING.
newsitem.headline: LLOYDS, BANKS HIT BY PROFIT TAKING.

text.p: Shares in Lloyds TSB Group Plc led other bank stocks lower on Friday, victim of profit taking after a week of strong gains that culminated with the UK interest rate hike on Thursday, traders said.
By 1214 GMT, Lloyds shares, which touched a record high 787-1/2p on Thursday, were off 32p or 4.11 percent at 746p.
Bank of Scotland shares lost 15p to 432p, Halifax Plc fell 12-1/2p to 734p and Barclays Plc 31-1/2p to 14.16 stg.
"I think it's probably profit taking after a strong run and people closing up for the week," said John Leonard, European banking analyst at Salomon Brothers.
Leonard said shares were also unsettled by weaker bank stocks in the U.S. on Thursday.
Financial stocks ended sharply lower as yields on the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury continued to edge higher, to 6.52 percent.
The Bank of England's move to hike interest rates to 7.0 percent from 6.75 percent bolstered UK bank shares on Thursday, amid views inflation was being contained and securing a benign environment.
"It's just the financial stocks that are getting hit," one trader said. "Lloyds does stand out a bit but it could well be just profit taking."
